title: Tencent-backed chipmaker Enflame nearly triples in its Shanghai debut
content:
Shares in Shanghai Enflame Technology closed 179% above their offer price on their first day of trading on Shanghai’s Star Market on Friday. The Tencent-backed AI chipmaker had raised about 6.12bn yuan ($911m) in its initial public offering, Bloomberg reported.
The stock opened at 410 yuan, against an IPO price of 142.18 yuan. It rose as much as 234% to 475 yuan during the day before closing at 397 yuan, Ann Cao reported for the South China Morning Post. That gave Enflame a market value of 170.9bn yuan ($25.5bn), according to the SCMP. Reports published during the session gave other figures: CNBC put the gain at 206%, and Business Insider at about 200%.
The wider market fell. The Star 50 Index dropped 1% on Friday and the benchmark CSI 300 Index 0.8%, the SCMP reported.
Demand for the shares
Retail investors bid for 4,073 times the shares available to them, according to Enflame’s filing to the exchange, cited by the SCMP. About 7 million online investors ordered 42.1bn shares. Individual investors got an allocation rate of 0.025%, one of the lowest in mainland China this year. The robot maker Unitree had a rate of 0.018%, the SCMP reported.
CNBC gave a higher figure. It reported that the retail offering drew orders for more than 6,000 times the shares available, before Enflame reallocated more stock to that group. Enflame sold 43 million shares in the IPO, according to Bloomberg. It won approval for the listing in June.
Who runs Enflame
Enflame was founded in Shanghai in 2018 and makes AI chips for training and inference. It has fewer than 900 employees and has never turned a profit, Diana Li reported for Bloomberg. The company takes its name from a Chinese mythical figure credited with inventing fire.
Its co-founders, Zhao Lidong and Zhang Yalin, both worked at AMD. Zhao spent two decades in Silicon Valley and was a vice president at the state-backed Tsinghua Unigroup. Zhang rose through AMD’s Shanghai research centre to run its core chip development, according to Bloomberg.
From the start, the founders chose not to compete directly with Nvidia’s general-purpose graphics processors. They built a different type of chip, designed to work outside Nvidia’s ecosystem, Bloomberg reported. The share rise brought each founder’s fortune to $2.5bn, according to Bloomberg. Both are bound by long lockup periods and must meet certain targets before they can sell. Enflame did not respond to Bloomberg’s requests for comment.
Tencent and the numbers
Tencent holds a 20% stake in Enflame and is also its largest customer. Sales to Tencent made up 84% of Enflame’s revenue in 2025, up from about 38% a year earlier, according to Bloomberg. The chips run in large data centres, powering chatbots, recommendation systems and generative AI.
Revenue rose to 990m yuan in 2025, from 722m yuan in 2024, CNBC reported. Enflame posted a net loss of 1.16bn yuan for 2025, narrower than the 1.5bn yuan loss the year before, according to Bloomberg. The company forecast a loss of no more than 860m yuan for the first nine months of 2026. Bloomberg reported that revenue for the period is expected to more than triple from a year earlier. Enflame expects to break even in 2026 or 2027, Business Insider reported.
Enflame plans to spend the proceeds on developing its fifth- and sixth-generation AI chips, according to CNBC. It wants them to match the performance of high-end products from international rivals.
What analysts said
“The appeal of the company lies in its position as one of China’s leading cloud AI chipmakers, as well as Tencent’s dual role as both a key customer and major shareholder,” analysts at Huajin Securities, including Li Hui, wrote in a note, Bloomberg reported. They added that Enflame trails its peers in revenue scale and gross margin.
Paul Triolo, a partner and head of technology at the advisory firm DGA, called Enflame’s choice of alternative chips a “high-risk form of strategic independence”. He told Bloomberg that the approach “may be good for Tencent and municipal data centers”. It could be “less attractive in the open developer market”, he said.
Where its chips are made
Enflame still relies on overseas manufacturers to produce its advanced chips, Qianer Liu reported for The Information. In late 2023, geopolitical tensions forced it to downgrade some chip designs to keep access to TSMC’s factories, according to Bloomberg. To bring in revenue, it has relied on Chinese state-backed computing projects in cities such as Wuxi and Qingyang.
The other ‘little dragons’
Enflame is the last of China’s “four little dragons” of AI chipmaking to list. The other three are Moore Threads, MetaX and Biren. MetaX soared nearly 700% on its first day of trading in December, CNBC reported. Moore Threads rose 425% on its debut the same month, according to Bloomberg, and has since planned a Hong Kong listing. Biren jumped 76% on its listing in January.
CNBC and Bloomberg described those shares differently. According to CNBC, all three have remained above their listing prices. Bloomberg reported that they have all fallen back substantially. Moore Threads is down more than 60% from its record high, and MetaX and Biren more than 40% from their peaks, according to Bloomberg.
Other Chinese chip listings have also surged on debut. In July, the memory maker CXMT rose nearly 466% on its Shanghai debut, CNBC reported.
China’s push to replace Nvidia
International chipmakers led by Nvidia held nearly 60% of China’s AI accelerator market in 2025. CNBC cited that IDC figure from Enflame’s prospectus. US export controls and Beijing’s lukewarm interest in importing advanced chips have shut off Nvidia’s exports to China’s data centre market, according to CNBC. Z.ai said its GLM-5.3-Flash model runs entirely on China-made chips. Analysts said it likely used chips from Huawei, Enflame and other local companies, CNBC reported.
China is “still at a very early stage of a multi-year IPO upcycle”, Morgan Stanley analysts wrote in a note on 28 August, Business Insider reported. Many of the new listings are developing technologies China sees as strategically important, though many are not yet profitable, the bank said. “Capital markets are therefore critical to help them scale up,” its analysts wrote. Goldman Sachs expects China’s semiconductor capital spending to reach $82bn by 2030, according to CNBC.

report.summary: 腾讯系AI芯片公司燧原科技科创板首日暴涨179%
report.background: 燧原科技2018年成立于上海，创始团队出自AMD，主攻训练与推理AI芯片，刻意绕开英伟达的通用GPU路线，构建独立生态。它是中国AI芯片「四小龙」中最后一家上市的公司，摩尔线程、沐曦、壁仞此前已相继登陆资本市场。在美国出口管制收紧、英伟达数据中心业务基本退出中国的背景下，国产算力成为科创板最热赛道，资本正密集押注这一替代叙事。
key_points: 首日暴涨：发行价142.18元，开盘410元，盘中最高触及475元，收盘397元，涨幅179%，市值约255亿美元。
腾讯既是股东又是大客户：持股20%，2025年84%的收入来自腾讯，而前一年这一比例仅约38%，客户集中度极高。
仍未盈利：2025年营收9.9亿元、净亏11.6亿元，公司预计2026或2027年扭亏，募资将投向第五、六代芯片研发。
打新狂热：网上投资者超额认购超4000倍，中签率仅0.025%，为今年内地最低之一，散户几乎抢不到货。
隐忧仍在：先进芯片依赖台积电代工，2023年曾被迫降级设计；分析师称其独立生态在开放开发者市场吸引力有限。
report.impact: 对AI行业：进一步强化国产算力替代叙事，科创板正成为硬科技公司的主要融资渠道，但估值与基本面脱节的风险也在累积。对开发者：多了一个非CUDA的选择，但软件栈迁移成本和生态成熟度仍需实测权衡。对普通用户：短期感受不到变化，长期则影响国内AI服务的算力成本与供给稳定性。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注燧原自研的驭算TopsRider软件栈，并对比华为CANN、摩尔线程MUSA、沐曦MACAU等国产生态，以及vLLM、SGLang等推理框架的国产芯片适配分支；实际跑一轮模型迁移测试，是判断生态成熟度最直接的方式。
